statement: The Building Safety Regulator's gateway process has lengthened the time between obtaining planning approval and starting on site by around twelve months.
planning_data_link: Second-staircase redesigns on Berkeley sites from 2023 onwards

statement: Berkeley is not proposing to acquire new land while these conditions prevail, except through joint venture arrangements, and will focus on its existing land holdings; the Berkeley 2035 target is to add £2 billion of value to them through optimisation and planning.
planning_data_link: New applications are mostly re-plans of land already held

statement: More than 40 planning amendments were agreed to existing consents for additional homes, including at Bow Green, White City Living, TwelveTrees Park, London Dock and Heron Wharf.
planning_data_link: Amendment volumes held up while new schemes and condition discharges fell

statement: The Planning Inspectorate blocked plans for over 850 homes in Peckham; Beckton Gasworks and Motspur Park Gasworks were blocked at local level and called in by the GLA.
planning_data_link: Aylesham Centre appeal dismissed; Motspur Park called in; Beckton still awaiting a decision in the data

statement: It now takes at least eight years to complete an apartment building in London from acquisition, against five years a decade ago, with a further 18 months for an appeal or call-in.
planning_data_link: Median time to decide a major London housing application has roughly doubled since 2019

statement: Berkeley Living, the build-to-rent platform, holds 1,122 homes across six buildings, including Alexandra Gate, Kidbrooke Village, Grand Union and Silkstream.
planning_data_link: Market-rent homes appear in Berkeley applications from 2023 (Seagas House, TwelveTrees Park, Royal Arsenal)

statement: Berkeley is reducing production by around 25% over the next four years, putting cash generation ahead of short-term profit targets.
planning_data_link: Condition discharges, the construction-activity proxy, are below their 2019-25 range
